title: The route to chaos
summary: From a limit cycle to period doubling and chaos: read Poincaré sections and draw a bifurcation diagram.

steps.title: A limit cycle
steps.text:
The Van der Pol oscillator pumps energy in at small amplitude (negative damping for |x| < 1) and takes it out at large amplitude. Whatever the start, it settles on one closed loop in the phase plane: a limit cycle.

Run it and look at the Phase portrait, then read the Limit-cycle amplitude in the Summary.

check.success: About 2, whatever the start: try x0 = 3 and the motion shrinks onto the same loop.

steps.title: Period-1
steps.text:
Now a damped pendulum driven by a torque A cos ωt (q = 2, ω = 2/3, as in Baker and Gollub's Chaotic Dynamics). A Poincaré section looks at the motion once per drive period, like a strobe light. If the motion repeats every period, the strobe always sees the same state: one point.

Run A = 0.9 and open the Poincaré map.

check.success: One point: the motion repeats every drive period.

steps.title: Period doubling
steps.text: Drive a little harder, A = 1.07, and run. The motion now takes two drive periods to repeat, and the strobe sees two points: a period-doubling bifurcation.

check.success: Two points: period-2. The Spectrum tab now has a peak at ω/2 too.

steps.title: Chaos
steps.text: At A = 1.5 the motion never repeats. The pendulum swings and goes over the top in an irregular pattern, and the strobe points fill a folded, fractal shape: a strange attractor. Run it and look at the Poincaré map and the Animation.

check.success: Every point is new: chaos. Change the start by 0.001 rad and the motion soon differs completely.

steps.title: The bifurcation diagram
steps.text: Put it all together: the Analyze ▸ Sweep tab is set up to vary the drive from A = 0.9 to 1.5 in 121 steps. Run the sweep (it takes a minute or two) and plot "Poincaré θ (all values)": every run's section points above its value of A. Read it from left to right: one branch, a split into two near A = 1.07, and within about 0.02 chaos, with windows of order further on (period-1 near A = 1.35, then period-2 and period-4 again near 1.45 and 1.47). Every run starts from rest, so where two motions coexist the diagram shows the one reached from rest: at A = 1.08 a period-3 motion, rather than the period-4 that follows the period-2 when A is raised slowly.
